item.title: Kunozan Toshogu: The Original Resting Place of Tokugawa Ieyasu — Guide
item.description: Kunozan Toshogu is the original shrine of Tokugawa Ieyasu, founder of the Tokugawa shogunate, built on Mount Kuno overlooking Suruga Bay immediately after his death in 1616 as his first burial place, before his remains were later enshrined at the more famous Nikko. Its brilliantly ornate halls, decorated with lacquer, gold leaf and intricate carvings, are designated National Treasures and predate Nikko’s, and the shrine is reached either by a scenic ropeway from the Nihondaira plateau or by climbing more than 1,100 stone steps up from the coast below.
